### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via AuthManagerOptions (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `84cc243f8d1c3e297bd3fbeba8ae3f87114407a7` — the merge of head `4ca69113ccc4c642ec5bc1a000a5884302dd8ac3` into base `cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 84cc243f8d1c3e297bd3fbeba8ae3f87114407a7 && git checkout 84cc243f8d1c3e297bd3fbeba8ae3f87114407a7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73 4ca69113ccc4c642ec5bc1a000a5884302dd8ac3 && git checkout -B drift-repro cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73 && git merge --no-ff 4ca69113ccc4c642ec5bc1a000a5884302dd8ac3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd55df8f3ce5beb41f4db51ef3b7eb7ac317dd73` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:cloud#5 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPP1zuWBNq3nBXVei9

**ACCEPT** 2026-11-20T19:40Z · head `4ca69113ccc4` · Fixes #35829

**Review history.** The independent review of the first head returned FAIL on one blocker, B1: `SessionCreateBeforeResult.data` was optional, so it did not match better-auth's hook result, and a hook written from the documented example failed strict type-checking. The test hid this behind `as any`. The same review passed the security logic:
- the candidates add no access, and each one is judged by the same organization-policy path;
- if every candidate is refused, the sign-in is refused;
- with no list, behaviour is unchanged;
- judging a candidate signs out no other session.

The seat re-read the rework delta (`931c80aaca1..4ca69113ccc`):
- **B1, fixed.** `data: TSession` is required, and the default type argument matches better-auth's `Record<string, any>`. Two typed fixtures, the documented example and a list-only hook, are assigned to `AuthManagerOptions['databaseHooks']` without a cast and also run at runtime. A `@ts-expect-error` pins that a result without `data` is refused. The dev's ablation: making `data?` optional turns `check:test-typecheck` red, and restore was byte-equal.
- **N1, done.** When two candidates are both admitted, the earlier one wins, asserted in both orders. The ablation reverses the loop: that one case goes red, and restore was byte-equal.
- **N3, done.** The exported interface's JSDoc, which ships in `.d.ts`, states the host's duty: list only organizations the user is a member of. It also states the consequence of a non-member candidate: the per-request `vetOrganizationClaim` drops the claim.
- **N4, done.** The `autoActiveOrganization` JSDoc says the default stays out once the host returns a list.
- **ADR-0093 D9.** The "only when the draft lacks one" drift is left in the ADR, which is governed. The seat files it as a separate card.

**Gates.** All check-runs on `4ca69113ccc4` are green or a skip by design. The dev ran 76 derived gate families: 75 exited 0, and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was left to CI because it needs the whole repo built. The plugin-auth package: typecheck clean, and 6129 tests passed.

**Out of scope.** GHSA-hgg7-484f-w5x9 is handled privately and is not touched by this PR. The ADR-0093 drift card follows.

**Landing.** The path surface is `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/**` plus a changeset: not governed, and under 3000 lines. The seat lands it: ready, then auto-merge.
